title: Her research has been cited 27,000 times. In 2026, one of science's oldest honors caught up.
sources: Brown University, March 25, 2026 - Brown engineering dean elected AAAS Fellow
American Bazaar, April 6, 2026 - Indian American researcher Tejal Desai elected AAAS fellow
caption:
Her research has been cited 27,000 times by peers worldwide. In 2026, one of science's oldest honors finally caught up.

Tejal Desai, Dean of Engineering at Brown University, was elected a Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science in 2026. The daughter of an Indian immigrant chemical engineer, she built her career applying micro and nanoscale technology to deliver medicine precisely inside the human body - over 300 research papers, 30+ patents and membership in three separate US National Academies: Medicine, Engineering and Inventors.

A father's engineering career, one generation later, became a daughter's seat in three national academies at once.
